ui.models.dont-use-nomi-config-use-this-: Don't use Nomi's config; use this computer's login for {0}

ui.models.search-vendors-relay-platforms: Search vendors, relay platforms or local services
ui.models.any-service-compatible-with-th: Any service compatible with the Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini APIs
ui.models.a-root-address-v1-or-a-full-v1: A root address, /v1 or a full /v1/chat/completions all work; Nomi finds the address for each API automatically.
ui.models.one-per-line-the-first-is-the-: One per line; the first is the primary key, the rest are backups in order
ui.models.local-services-don-t-need-a-ke: Local services don't need a key.
ui.models.no-api-is-available-so-this-ca: No API is available, so this can't be saved. Check the reason on each line above.
ui.models.one-third-party-provider-can-s: One third-party provider can serve Nomi chat and every coding assistant at once; Nomi converts between APIs automatically. Official account sign-in and switching stay on the Coding assistants page.
ui.models.is-a-local-or-lan-address-allo: “{0}” is a local or LAN address. Allow Nomi to access it?
ui.models.if-the-service-doesn-t-list-it: If the service doesn't list its models, this model name is used for detection and added to the model list.
ui.models.no-model-list-was-returned-go-: No model list was returned. Go back and enter a test model.
ui.models.no-third-party-providers-yet-a: No third-party providers yet. Add one and Nomi chat can use its models.
ui.models.delete-provider-and-all-its-ke: Delete provider “{0}” and all its keys?
ui.models.can-t-be-decrypted-please-ente: {0} can't be decrypted. Please enter it again.
ui.models.lists-the-models-enabled-under: Lists the models enabled under Settings → Models.
ui.models.no-models-to-switch-to-yet-add: No models to switch to yet. Add a third-party provider under Settings → Models first.
ui.models.each-coding-assistant-tab-can-: New tabs can use "Default" (the CLI's own config), "Official" (Nomi's managed official account, with an account you can choose), or "Third-party" (a provider configured through Nomi). Set the default third-party model here; the CLI's global config is not changed.
ui.models.third-party-reasoning-can-t-be: Third-party reasoning can't be sent to the official API, so this will continue in a new session that carries the context. The original session is kept. Continue?
ui.models.this-tab-uses-a-third-party-mo: This tab uses a third-party model (through the Nomi gateway).
ui.models.official-uses-the-cli-s-own-ac: "Official" uses the CLI's own account; "Third-party" goes through the Nomi gateway. Only the current tab is affected, starting with the next message.
ui.models.clis-in-your-terminal-are-back: CLIs in your terminal are back to your own config and official login. Third-party models are now used in Nomi's tabs (pick "Third-party" at the top right).
ui.models.couldn-t-undo-the-third-party-: Couldn't undo the third-party settings an earlier version wrote into {0}'s global config: {1}. Please check it manually; Nomi will retry on next launch.
ui.models.s-responses-api-rejects-custom: {0}'s Responses API rejects custom tools; converting instead
ui.models.delete-this-takes-effect-when-: Delete {0}? This takes effect when you save.
ui.models.this-provider-comes-from-envir: This provider comes from environment variables and is read-only. To change it, edit the environment variables and restart Nomi.
ui.models.can-t-be-decrypted-enter-it-ag: Can't be decrypted; enter it again
ui.models.paste-the-new-key-it-replaces-: Paste the new key; it replaces {0} when you save
ui.models.this-name-looks-like-a-key-the: This name looks like a key. The name is only a label; it doesn't change the key used for requests.
ui.models.use-it-to-replace-this-key-ins: Use it to replace this key instead
ui.models.add-keys-one-per-line-placed-a: Add keys: one per line, placed after the existing keys in order
ui.models.when-this-provider-s-models-al: When this provider's models all fail, use the models below in order.
ui.models.address-per-api-leave-empty-to: Address per API (leave empty to turn that API off)
ui.models.the-addresses-changed-detectin: The addresses changed; detecting again is recommended.
ui.models.restrict-models-to-apis-none-c: Restrict models to APIs (none checked = automatic)
ui.models.model-mapping-model-name-in-th: Model mapping (model name in the request → model name sent upstream)
ui.models.use-third-party-models-in-a-te: Use third-party models in a terminal with commands such as nomi-claude and nomi-codex; running claude or codex directly still uses your official sign-in.
ui.models.added-to-path-takes-effect-in-: Added to PATH (takes effect in new terminals): {0}
ui.models.added-to-your-user-path-restar: Added to your user PATH (restart your terminal app to apply)
ui.models.nomi-will-add-the-command-fold: Nomi will add the command folder to your user PATH. Turning this off removes only the folder Nomi added, preserving existing entries and other environment variables.
ui.models.not-on-path-yet-run-the-comman: Not on PATH yet. Run the commands by full path, or add the folder to PATH.
ui.models.on-windows-nomi-doesn-t-change: On Windows, Nomi doesn't change PATH. Add the folder above to your user PATH environment variable manually.
ui.models.nomi-will-append-a-marked-bloc: Nomi will append a marked block to the end of the files below that adds the command folder to PATH. The block is removed when you turn this off; nothing else is changed.
ui.models.used-for-helper-requests-such-: Used for helper requests such as titles, summaries and next-prompt suggestions; usually a cheaper model from the same provider
ui.models.key-limits-leave-blank-for-no-: Key limits (leave blank for no limit; extra requests queue, then move to the next key)
ui.models.when-on-parameters-the-model-d: When on, parameters the model doesn't support (such as reasoning effort or temperature) cause an error; when off, the gateway removes or adjusts them and notes it in Recent requests
ui.models.posts-over-the-limit-get-413-d: POSTs over the limit get 413; default 32 MiB, adjustable from 1–256 MiB
